bsm_reauthorize_done_message: This job can run automatically again. The earlier failure remains in history; the next successful backup will update its status.
aunl_authorize_what: Enter the archive password or recovery key for {name}. The program will be able to run it automatically again. Existing backups and their recovery key are preserved.
cl_lead: Removes the temporary files, error reports, dumps, logs and caches programs and the system leave behind, and the traces of work — browser history, recent documents. The removal is plain and fast: the files do not go to the trash and cannot be brought back.
cl_users_hint: Temporary files, caches, the Recycle Bin and traces are cleaned for the ticked users.
cl_item_admin_only: Only a computer's administrator may remove it; its size shows anyway.
cl_elevate_hint: Windows components and other users' folders are cleaned only by a computer's administrator. If you have an administrator's password, restart the window as that user.
cl_elevate_ask: Windows components are removed only by a computer's administrator. Restart the window as an administrator? Windows will ask for the password.
cl_admin_hint_linux: System items (apt, logs, snap) and other users' folders are cleaned only by an administrator: root or a member of the sudo group.
clp_row_none: What is ticked can be saved under a name of your own and chosen in a copy's settings: the disk is then cleaned by it before the copy.
clp_row_saved: Saved: {names}. Chosen in a copy's settings, the Cleanup tab.
clp_lead: What is ticked on the page now is saved, for the ticked users, with the history kept. The profile is chosen in a copy's settings (the Cleanup tab): before the copy the service cleans the disk by it.
clp_nothing: Nothing is ticked — tick items on the page and open this window again.
clp_pick_title: Take this name — save over it
clp_open_title: Tick this profile's items and users on the page
cla_summary_off: off — the service cleans by itself only on a schedule or before a copy
cla_lead: The service cleans by itself, with no window, on a schedule. What is ticked on the page now is cleaned, for the ticked users, with the same ages and options. Jobs with "Clean the disk before the copy" that chose no cleanup profile take this set too.
cla_run_missed: If the computer was off — run the missed cleanup after it starts
cla_nothing: Nothing is ticked — tick items on the page and open this window again.
cla_left: Not included (removed only after looking through the list): {names}
cla_note: Each automatic cleanup's result goes into Activity. The set is saved by whoever presses Save, with their rights: Windows components and other users' folders — a computer's administrator only.
cla_note_linux: Each automatic cleanup's result goes into Activity. The set is saved by whoever presses Save, with their rights: system items and other users' folders — an administrator only (root or a member of the sudo group).
wiz_adv_cleanup_before: Clean the disk before the copy
wiz_adv_cleanup_before_hint: Before each copy the service cleans the disk by the chosen cleanup profile: no junk goes into the copy. If the cleanup cannot run, the copy is made anyway.
wiz_cleanup_no_profiles: No profiles of your own yet. Create one in Cleanup: tick the items and press Save profile as… below the list.
wiz_cleanup_profile_gone_note: The chosen profile is no longer there — nothing will be cleaned before the copy. Choose another.
wiz_cleanup_profile_empty: The profile has no items — there is nothing to clean before the copy. Save it again in Cleanup.
wiz_cleanup_set_empty: The automatic cleanup set is empty — there is nothing to clean before the copy. Choose a profile or set the automatic set in Cleanup → Automatic cleanup settings.
wiz_cleanup_set_where: Profiles are saved in the Cleanup section with Save profile as…; the automatic cleanup set is there too, under Automatic cleanup settings. Files by masks are not part of them.
cl_step_masks: Choose the masks ({count} chosen) — the item ticks itself.
cl_step_analyze: Press Analyse — the program finds the files by the masks.
cl_step_review: Look through the files found and untick the ones you need.
cl_step_nothing: The analysis found nothing — there is nothing to remove.
cl_step_clean: Press Clean up below and confirm with Remove.
clm_note: A mask is a file name only: * is any characters, ? one character. Masks too broad (*.*, *.d*) are refused. Backups, logs and files a disk check recovered are off by default — they may hold your data.
cl_junk_bad_mask: The mask "{mask}" will not do: a file name only, and one that does not take ordinary files — documents, photos, programs (as *.*, *.d* or K* would).
cl_junk_no_masks: At least one mask is needed.
cl_junk_pick: A folder to search for junk
cl_junk_folders_admin: The search runs through the ticked users' profiles. Other folders and drives can be added by a computer's administrator.
cl_review_first: Look through the list of "{names}" first: press Analyse, then the item's Files — and untick the files you need.
cl_confirm: These files cannot be brought back: they do not go to the Recycle Bin.
cl_hint_start: Tick what to clean and press “Analyse” to see how much space it frees.
cl_hint_done_left: Freed: {size}. {count} files ({left}) stayed — programs have them open.
cl_pick_item: Pick an item to see what it removes.
cl_files_title: See which files will be removed
cl_stale: The users or the days of history kept changed — press “Analyse” to see what will be removed.
clf_truncated: The list holds the first 1,000,000 files — the cleanup removes only those.
clf_note: The cleanup removes exactly these files when the item is ticked: those that turned up after the analysis stay, and so do the unticked ones. Changing the users, the days of history kept or the masks needs a new analysis.
app_engine_down: The engine is not responding. Start it: own-backup-service.exe --run --media, then click “Retry”.
app_engine_down_linux: The engine is not responding. Start it: own-backup-service --run --media, then click “Retry”.
app_not_installed_temp: The “Own Backup” service is not installed (a temporary instance is answering now). Install it: own-backup-service.exe /install — otherwise schedules will not run.
app_not_installed_temp_linux: The “Own Backup” service is not installed (a temporary instance is answering now). Install the own-backup package (sudo apt install ./own-backup_*.deb) — otherwise schedules will not run.
app_not_installed: The “Own Backup” service is not installed. The program needs it: run own-backup-service.exe /install (you will be asked for administrator rights), then click “Retry”.
app_not_installed_linux: The “Own Backup” service is not installed. The program needs it: install the own-backup package (sudo apt install ./own-backup_*.deb), grant yourself access (sudo /usr/libexec/own-backup/own-backup-service --grant-access $USER), log in again (that puts you in the own-backup group) and click “Retry”.
app_stopped: The “Own Backup” service is installed but not running. Start it (administrator rights are needed) or restart the computer, then click “Retry”.
app_stopped_linux: The “Own Backup” service is installed, but the window cannot connect to it. If it is not running — sudo systemctl start own-backup; if it is, your user is probably not in the own-backup group yet: log in again. Then click “Retry”.
app_access_denied: The service refuses this window: it accepts commands only from the active local session (at this computer) or from root. A window started over SSH or from a remote or inactive session is not allowed — open the program in your own session at this computer and click “Retry”.
set_data_dir_help: Jobs, logs and the program's working files live here. Backups are stored wherever each job says.
set_compression_help: zstd compression for qcow2 and OBK backups — for jobs without a level of their own (“Scheme” in the job's options). VHDX is not compressed. The higher the level, the smaller the file and the longer the backup; 3 is a sensible balance, above 9 backups get noticeably slower for little gain in size. Takes effect from the next run.
set_log_level_help: The verbose log is for when something went wrong and you need to know why; it is noticeably bigger. Applied on the fly — no need to restart the service.
set_log_mirror: Mirror the log to a disk
set_log_mirror_placeholder: e.g. {example} — leave empty not to mirror
set_log_mirror_help: A copy of the service and window logs goes to this folder — a USB stick or another disk.
set_theme_help: “Same as the system” follows the system's light or dark mode setting and switches along with it.
set_language_help: “Same as the system”: Russian if the system is in Russian, English otherwise.
set_service_offline: The service is not running or not responding.
set_service_refused: The service is running but refuses this window: only windows from the active local session (at this computer) or run as root are accepted.
set_tray_help: The icon next to the clock is shown while the service is running and appears when you sign in to Windows. Clicking it opens this window.
set_tray_help_linux: The icon in the notification area is shown while the service is running and appears when you log in. Its menu has «Open Own Backup». GNOME shows such icons only with the AppIndicator extension (enabled in Ubuntu).
set_mount_no_nbd: the NBD module is not loaded
set_mount_no_ntfs: ready, but NTFS is not supported — ntfs-3g is needed
set_mount_ready_on_demand: ready; the iSCSI service starts on demand
dash_phase_exclusions: Removing excluded files from the image…
dash_phase_finalize: Finishing: writing the image to disk…
dash_excluding_note: deleting and zeroing the files in the finished backup…
dash_finalizing_note: flushing the cache to disk, hold on…
dash_release_note: the image is written, the volume snapshot is being released…
dash_opening_note: opening the finished backup for the removal…
dash_src_encrypted_plain: The source is an encrypted volume. The copy holds it decrypted, and the copy itself is not encrypted.
dash_src_encrypted_sealed: The source is an encrypted volume. The copy holds it decrypted, inside the encrypted archive.
dash_stalled: The copy has not moved for {min} min. If the backup disk is failing or disconnected, the run can be cancelled.
dash_stalled_release: The volume snapshot has not been released for {min} min. The image is already written. This happens when a device or a service hangs in the system — a failing USB stick, for one.
dash_stalled_open: The backup has not opened for the removal of excluded files for {min} min. This happens when the system cannot attach a new disk — because of a hung USB device, for one.
dash_live_cats_head: What goes into the backup — by file type
dash_cats_about_text: The breakdown by type is counted from the files that went into the backup (by extension) while the volume is scanned. Excluded files are not counted.
dash_cats_skipped: The breakdown by type was not counted for this backup: {reason}.
dash_cats_next: The breakdown by type will appear after the next backup (it is counted while the volume is scanned).
dash_created_snapshot: Backup created — {kind}, from a volume snapshot (LVM/dm).
dash_consolidated: Versions consolidated: {count} — the oldest increments were merged into the full backup, which now matches a later day.
dash_entries_kept: Excluded files remain in the backup's catalog:
dash_excl_ignored_rest: ({rules}): {reason}. Everything they cover is in the backup.
run_error_reauthorize: The authorization for this job's automatic backups is missing or no longer opens. Authorize them again: job menu → "Authorize automatic backups again…".
run_error_key_protection: The service's key protection on this machine failed (TPM or systemd-creds). Authorizing the job again will not help: it needs the same protection. Check that the TPM is enabled and visible to the system (systemd-creds has-tpm2), then run the backup again.
bs_encrypted_title: This job's backups are encrypted — reading them needs the password or the recovery key
bs_delete_q: Are you sure you want to delete this job?
bs_delete_q_named: Are you sure you want to delete the job “{name}”?
bs_delete_warn: This backup's image files will be permanently deleted from the disk.
bs_deleted_partly: The job is deleted, but not all of its backups are:
bs_history_truncated: The run history is full: folders the job used earlier may not have been checked.
bsm_rename_note: Only the name in the list changes. The files on disk keep their names, and the version chain carries on.
jv_none: This backup has no versions on disk yet.
jvc_intro: Tick the versions to delete. A version built on a ticked one is deleted with it: it cannot be read without it.
jvc_warn_latest: The latest version is among the ticked ones. After the deletion the newest state of the disk can no longer be restored.
jvc_warn_all: Every version is ticked. After the deletion there is nothing to restore from, and the next backup will be a full one.
jvc_confirm: Delete from the backup “{name}” what is ticked: {versions}, {size}?
jvc_no_undo: The files are deleted from the disk for good.
jvc_unreadable: The folder {folder} could not be read:
jex_intro: The disk as of the chosen version is saved as one VHDX file: no chain, no compression, no encryption. Windows itself and any virtual machine open such a file.
jex_bad_name: A file name must not contain \ / : * ? " < > |
jex_not_encrypted: This job's backups are encrypted, but the saved file will NOT be: the data in it is in the clear.
jex_writing: Saving the disk to a file
jex_done: Done in {time}. The file takes {stored}; the disk in it is {size}.
jmt_intro: The chosen version is mounted read-only and its volumes get drive letters. The Tools section opens — the disk is unmounted there as well.
rl_empty_hint: Create them in “Backup” or click “Add backup”.
rl_encrypted_job_title: This job's backups are encrypted — reading them needs the password or the recovery key
rl_encrypted_copy_title: This backup is encrypted — reading it needs the password or the recovery key
rl_forget_title: Remove from the list (the files are not deleted)
rl_folder_sub: find all backups in the folder
rl_remember: Add the backup file(s) to the Backups list
rl_remember_sub: the backup stays in the list after a restart — no need to find the file again
rl_not_saved: The list of backups was not saved: {error}
rl_folder_empty: No backups with metadata were found in the chosen folder.
dmap_layout_only_title: in the backup: no file system, only its partition table entry is kept
dmap_unalloc_create: Unallocated — {size} (click to create a partition here)
dmap_unalloc_place: Unallocated — {size} (click to place the backup here)
dmap_absent_title: {name} — {size}: this partition is not in the backup
eng_no_volumes: No volume with a drive letter was found. Details are in own-backup-gui.log next to the exe.
wiz_err_no_volume: Choose a source (at least one volume on the disk).
wiz_err_no_disk: Choose the disk this backup will work with.
wiz_err_same_disk: A backup cannot be saved to the disk being backed up ({letter}:). Choose another disk for the destination.
wiz_err_decrypt_first: Unlock the selected encrypted volume first.
wiz_hint_pick_disk: Choose the disk this backup will work with
wiz_hint_cannot_open: Nothing can open volume “{label}” — untick it
wiz_hint_enter_rk: Enter the recovery key for volume “{label}”

wiz_enc_hint_mismatch: The backup passwords do not match
wiz_evt_dest_connected: When the disk the backup is written to is connected
wiz_seg_encrypted: Encrypted — a password will be needed
wiz_seg_layout_entry: included in the backup: there is no file system, only its partition table entry is kept
wiz_seg_msr: a Windows partition: included together with the Windows volume or the EFI partition
wiz_rk_wrong_length: A recovery key has 48 digits (8 groups of 6); you entered {count}
wiz_rk_bad_group: Group {n} (“{group}”) does not check out — a typo in the digits
wiz_pw_head_rk: Encrypted volumes — enter the recovery key
wiz_pw_head_pw: Encrypted volumes — enter the password to unlock them
wiz_pw_mapping_hint: An opened LUKS container reads as it is, but a copy while it is in use (a snapshot) needs the container's password — after cryptsetup open the key exists only in the kernel. Tick “remember” for scheduled copies.
wiz_pw_shared_title: All encrypted volumes share one password — enter it once and unlock them all
wiz_pw_shared_failed: The password did not work for: {volumes}. Untick “Shared password” to enter a password for each of these volumes.
wiz_pw_no_way: Nothing here can open it: {methods}. Own Backup opens a volume with a password or a recovery key — unlock it in the operating system or leave the volume out of the backup.
wiz_pw_rk_wrong: The recovery key does not match this volume
wiz_pw_rk_hint_before: The system volume has no password — only its 48-digit recovery key opens it. To find the key in a running Windows:
wiz_pw_rk_hint_after: — or on the Microsoft account page, in AD/Intune, or on a printout. Type it with dashes, with spaces or without either.
wiz_pw_locked_dropped: Volumes left locked will NOT go into the bootable backup — neither their data nor their partition table entry: on restore their space will be left free. Unlocked volumes go into the backup decrypted.
wiz_pw_general_hint: The volume's password or its 48-digit recovery key will do. The password is kept in memory until the program closes. “Remember” saves it in the OS's protected store — which a backup needs to run on a schedule.
wiz_src_sub_ro: partitions included in this backup (cannot be changed)
wiz_src_sub_volumes: now choose one or more volumes on the disk
wiz_src_sub_disk: first choose the disk it will work with
wiz_disks_unavailable: This backup's disks are not available right now (not connected) — the source cannot be shown.
wiz_boot_toggle_title: Mark the partitions the system boots from: EFI, the boot loader partition, the system partition itself. Data partitions are left alone — you choose those. An encrypted partition asks for its password first: while it is locked there is no telling whether it holds the system or data. The partition table (GPT) is kept either way — a disk backup is always one file.
wiz_boot_toggle_title_none: Nothing on this disk can boot — no EFI partition, no system, no encrypted volumes.

Enter the password below: if the system turns out to be inside, the volume joins the backup by itself. Leave a volume locked and it stays out of the backup; on restore its space will be left free.

wiz_boot_esp_only: Only an EFI partition was found on the disk — the system itself is not visible. If it is here, mark its partition by hand: without it the backup will not boot.
wiz_cat_head: What the backup holds — by file type
wiz_dest_sub: folder and file name of the backup
wiz_dest_collision: The destination is on the same disk ({letter}:) as one of the sources. The backup has to go to another disk — choose another folder.
wiz_sched_month_hint: The day of the month is 1–28 only: not every month has a 29th–31st, so those days cannot be chosen.
wiz_event_note: Events are watched by the “Own Backup” service.
wiz_event_dest_letter: The backup starts within 10 seconds after drive {letter}: appears. A disk connected before the service started does not count — only a new connection does.
wiz_event_dest_generic: The backup starts within 10 seconds after the destination disk appears. A disk connected before the service started does not count — only a new connection does.
wiz_event_dest_mount: The backup starts within 10 seconds after the volume {mount} is mounted — the desktop mounts it when the drive is plugged in, or /etc/fstab does. A volume mounted before the service started does not count — only a new connection.
wiz_event_dest_no_mount: The destination folder is not on a separately mounted volume right now: it is on the system disk, or its drive is not connected. The backup starts within 10 seconds after a volume is mounted under this folder; on the system disk this event never happens.
wiz_sched_service_note: Scheduled runs are started by the “Own Backup” service (it must be installed and running). For encrypted volumes, save the password on the “Source” step.
wiz_sched_wake_note: The computer wakes a minute before the run. Wake timers must be allowed in the power plan — on a laptop running on battery they are often off.
wiz_sched_run_missed: Run missed operations at system startup, with a delay (in minutes)
wiz_footer_remember_warn: One of the sources is an encrypted volume. For the backup to run on schedule, tick “Remember” for its password on the “Source” step — otherwise the service will skip the scheduled run.
wiz_format_already_encrypted: The job is already encrypted. Encryption cannot be turned off — the backups already made stay encrypted either way — and changing the key is done separately.
wiz_format_locked: The job already has backups — the format of an existing archive cannot be changed. For another format, create a new job.
wiz_obk_note: Our .obk container: compressed qcow2 inside, with every cluster sealed. The backups can be read only with this password or the recovery key — neither the service nor we can open them any other way. The program shows the recovery key once, when the job is saved; write it down.
wiz_qcow2_note: Built-in compression (zstd): a backup is usually 30–50 % smaller, and the saving shows at once. The same file opens the same way on Windows and Linux. Incremental and differential chains are supported. Restore, validation and mounting the backup as a disk all work. Excluded files are removed from the backup completely, NTFS/ReFS included — as with VHDX.
wiz_vhdx_note: Windows itself opens the backup with a double click and shows it as an ordinary disk — even without Own Backup. Incremental chains and full removal of excluded files (NTFS/ReFS). No compression — the file is bigger; on Linux it opens via qemu-nbd.
wiz_level_note: The higher the level, the smaller the file and the longer the backup. Above 9 backups get noticeably slower for little gain in size. Takes effect from the next run.
wiz_method_full_note: Every run makes a full backup: each backup stands on its own and restores without the others.
wiz_method_inc_note: Every run saves only the changes since the previous version (a chain: full → I1 → I2 …).
wiz_method_diff_note: Every run saves the changes since the full backup (full → D1, D2 …). Consolidation is not available for this method: every version rests directly on the full backup, and it cannot be moved without making the others wrong.
wiz_chain_note: Once the limit is reached, the next run makes a new full backup and starts a new chain. Old chains stay whole and are deleted by the rules below.
wiz_chain_points: Restore points: up to {n} per chain.
wiz_keep_first_copy: Do not delete the first (oldest) backup
wiz_keep_first_chain: Do not delete the first (oldest) chain
wiz_cleanup_note_copies: Old backups are deleted only after the next backup completes successfully. The backup just made is never deleted.
wiz_cleanup_note_chains: A chain is deleted whole — the full backup together with its versions — and only after the next backup completes successfully. The chain the latest backup belongs to is never deleted.
wiz_consol_note: No new full backup is made: once there are more versions than the limit, the oldest is merged into the full backup, and the next one rests directly on it. Space is saved, and a restore walks a short chain.
wiz_consol_points: Restore points: {total} — the full backup plus {n}.
wiz_consol_shift: But the full backup stops being a backup of the day it was made: it moves forward to the day of the merged version, and you can no longer roll back further.
wiz_restart_before: Start the chain over when it is older than
wiz_restart_note: A new full backup is made, and only after it completes successfully is the old chain deleted — there is never a moment without a backup. The chain's age counts from its start, not from the full backup's date: consolidation moves that forward every time.
wiz_no_restart_warn: The chain will never be refreshed: the same full backup stays the only copy of this data and is rewritten on every consolidation. One bad block in it takes all restore points at once. Turning the refresh on is recommended.
wiz_excl_note_masks: A mask without a path (*.tmp, pagefile.sys) applies across the whole volume; a mask with a path (Temp\*.log) — from the volume root. Exclusions do not apply in sector-by-sector mode.
wiz_excl_note_removal: Excluded files are removed from the backup completely: the space is freed both in the archive and on the restored volume. On NTFS and ReFS the data of excluded files never gets into the backup, and their directory entries in the finished image are deleted by the Windows file system driver itself; if that step fails, the files stay in the backup's directory empty (zeroed) — the backup is still fully usable.
wiz_excl_linux_note: For Linux partitions. Masks are from the volume root (/), e.g. var/cache/**. ext2/3/4 and btrfs — fully (the data stays out of the backup + the file is deleted from its directory). xfs — the data of excluded files stays out of the backup (the file itself still remains in its directory, empty, for now). On btrfs/xfs, files with shared extents (snapshots/reflink) are kept whole.
wiz_adv_validate_after: Validate the backup after it is made
wiz_adv_validate_latest_hint: Only the blocks this backup wrote are read, not the whole chain under it — on a long chain that is many times faster. But such a check will not notice damage in older backups, and without them the latest backup will not restore.
wiz_adv_enc_on_set: Backups are encrypted: OBK format, set in
wiz_adv_enc_on_pw: Backups are encrypted: OBK format; the password is set in
wiz_adv_enc_off: Backups are not encrypted. To set a password, choose the OBK format in
wiz_adv_retry_hint: For example, when the destination disk is not ready yet. A backup stopped by hand is not retried.
wiz_adv_after_shutdown_hint: Windows warns a minute and a half ahead; cancel with the command shutdown /a. Unsaved documents are not force-closed.
wiz_adv_after_shutdown_hint_linux: The system warns everyone logged in a minute and a half ahead; cancel with the command shutdown -c. Unsaved documents may be lost: programs close with the session.
wiz_adv_after_only_if: Only if no other backups are queued; not after a backup stopped by hand, and not while a retry is pending.
wiz_adv_low_priority: Low priority — stay out of the way
wiz_adv_low_priority_hint: Other programs get the disk and processor first: while the computer is busy, the backup runs slower.
wiz_adv_no_sleep: The computer does not go to sleep during a backup or a restore.
rd_step1: Step 1. Choose the disk to restore to — click it below.
rd_step2_whole: Step 2. Click the free (unallocated) space below — every partition of the backup will go there.
rd_step2_parts: Step 2. Click a partition above (it turns yellow), then the partition below to copy it to.
rd_step3: Step 3. Repeat for the other partitions and click “Restore”, or click “Cancel” to start over.
rd_fit_msr_no_data: The Microsoft Reserved partition (MSR) holds no data: the restore recreates it along with the partition table. You can map it — there is simply nothing in it to copy.
rd_fit_already_placed: The backup's partitions are already placed. Undo the last action to choose another place.
rd_fit_sector_mismatch: Incompatible geometry: the backup was taken from a disk with {src}-byte sectors, and the selected one has {dst}-byte sectors. A bootable backup cannot be moved without recomputing the layout. Choose a disk with {src}-byte sectors.
rd_fit_no_room: Not enough space: {need} needed, {free} free — {short} short. Delete partitions or choose another area.
rd_fit_size_too_small: The size is too small (minimum 1 MiB).
rd_fit_size_too_big: The size exceeds the free space ({free}).
rd_fit_whole_pick_free: In “bootable” mode, choose free space, not an existing partition.
rd_fit_too_small: This partition does not fit: ≥ {need} needed, {avail} available.
rd_fit_too_small_files: Onto a destination smaller than the source volume the data is copied file by file, but even that does not fit here.
rd_fit_step1: Step 1: choose the disk to restore to.
rd_fit_step2_whole: Step 2: choose free space for the backup's partitions.
rd_fit_step2_parts: Step 2: map at least one partition.
rd_fit_boot_sector: A bootable backup cannot be restored to a disk with {dst}-byte sectors (the backup was taken from {src}-byte ones).
rd_op_no_format_from_copy: no formatting: the file system comes from the backup
rd_op_restore_all: Restore every partition of the backup ({count} total, {size}) and the boot data
rd_op_msr: Partition {part} — recreated along with the partition table (the Microsoft Reserved partition holds no data)
rd_op_by_files: file by file: the destination is smaller than the source
rd_op_by_sectors: sector by sector, the whole partition is overwritten
rd_blocked_unchecked: The plan has not been checked — it cannot be run.
rd_blocked_luks: Enter the container password and click “Check”.
rd_made_by_unknown: Backup made by Own Backup — version not recorded (a build older than 0.1.1)
rd_key_note: This backup is encrypted. Until the password is entered, the map below is drawn from the job's settings, not from the backup itself, and the backup cannot be restored.
rd_key_note_no_map: This backup is encrypted. Its disk map is stored inside it — enter the password to see it and restore the backup.
rd_key_note_encryption: Whether the partitions come back encrypted shows once the password is entered.
rd_disk_not_connected: The disk with this backup is not connected — the map cannot be shown.
rd_luks_note: The container header is kept in the backup. The partition will be restored exactly as it was — the same UUID, the same password — and the system will boot without a single fix. The password is not stored in the backup: it is only needed to open the header and encrypt the data again. Leave the field empty and the partition will be restored without encryption; you will be warned about the consequences before the run.
rd_luks_plain_fs: Without encryption the partition will hold a plain file system with no container.
rd_luks_no_boot_html: The data will be intact and readable, but Linux will not boot from this partition: initramfs and /etc/crypttab expect an encrypted device that no longer exists. You will need a Live CD to remove the entry from /etc/crypttab, point /etc/fstab at the partition's own UUID and rebuild initramfs.
rd_enc_lost_title: The encryption will not be restored.
rd_enc_lost_one: Partition {part} was encrypted{kind}, but went into the backup decrypted.
rd_enc_lost_many: Partitions {parts} were encrypted{kind}, but went into the backup decrypted.
rd_bitlocker_boots_html: The data will be intact and readable, and Windows will boot from this partition — its loader is fine with decrypted NTFS. But the disk will stay unprotected: after the restore, turn BitLocker back on (“Control Panel” → “BitLocker Drive Encryption”), otherwise a copy of your data lies in the open.
rd_bitlocker_no_header: The BitLocker header is not kept in the backup, and Own Backup cannot put the encryption back during a restore yet — Windows does that itself.
rd_luks_no_header: This backup does not keep the container header — that is how backups used to be written. The next backups of this job will keep it, and then the partition will be restored together with its encryption.
rd_enc_unknown_html: The data will be intact and readable, but the volume will be restored without encryption — the backup did not record what kind of container it was (that is how backups used to be written). If it was BitLocker, turn it back on after the restore. If it was LUKS, the system will not boot from this partition until the entry is removed from /etc/crypttab and initramfs is rebuilt.
rd_cat_head: What's in the backup — by file type
rd_where_sub_disk: click the disk to restore to
rd_where_sub_part: click the partition to copy to
rd_searching_disks: Looking for disks to restore to…
rd_sector_body_html: The backup was taken from a disk with {src}-byte logical sectors; the selected disk has {dst}-byte ones. GPT stores partition positions as sector numbers (LBA), so on this disk the same layout would mean different byte offsets — it cannot be reproduced one-to-one.
rd_sector_whole: A bootable backup cannot be restored here: choose a disk with {src}-byte sectors.
rd_sector_parts: Individual partitions can be restored, but the boot chain will have to be repaired separately.
rd_hint_whole: Right-click a partition or free space to create / delete a partition.
rd_hint_parts: Click free space to create a partition. Right-click a partition to extend or delete it.
rd_hint_backup_busy: A backup is running — restore is unavailable.
rd_hint_default: The latest backup is restored. For individual files, use “Tools → Mount image as a disk”.
rd_del_body_html: Partition {name} — {size}. The space will become unallocated.
rd_align_note: The start of the partition is aligned to 1 MiB — otherwise every write would touch two physical sectors and run half as fast.
rd_check_failed_note: The queue of operations is below, but it has not been checked.
rd_check_ok: The checks found nothing in the way.
rd_letter_reassigned: Partition {part}: letter {requested}: is taken — {assigned}: will be assigned.
rd_letter_none: Partition {part}: letter {requested}: is taken — no free letters left.
rd_ops_title: The following operations will be performed
rd_wipe_note: only used blocks are copied, so the old data physically remains in the gaps — the file system does not see it
rd_verify_after: Verify the written data after the restore
rd_identity_keep: Keep them as they are (the copy will carry the same UUIDs and labels as this machine's devices)
rd_identity_change: Change them on the restored copy
rd_identity_change_fix: Change them and fix the restored system's fstab, crypttab and boot loader
rd_identity_change_fix_note: PARTUUIDs are not changed; if the initramfs keeps old UUIDs (LUKS, RAID), it will have to be rebuilt — the report will say so.
rd_edited_files_head: Fixed in the restored system (new identities):
rd_point_of_no_return: Next, the data on the disk will be overwritten. This cannot be undone.
rd_boot_intro: The backup holds this machine's boot menu — what the firmware offers at power-on. It lives in the motherboard's memory, not on the disk, so it is not restored along with the partitions.
rd_boot_vars: Firmware variables in total: {count}. The current entries will be saved to a file before they are replaced.
rd_boot_other_machine: The backup was taken on another machine (“{machine}”; this one is “{this_machine}”). The entries point to partitions by their GUID, and this machine may not have them — the items will appear in the menu but will not work.
rd_confirm_body_html: The layout of disk {disk} and the data of the mapped partitions will be overwritten with backup {job} from {date}.
rd_no_undo_rest: Everything now on the affected partitions will be lost.
tools_mounted_msg: Mounted ({mode}): {where}. You can open it in File Explorer.
tools_mounted_msg_linux: Mounted ({mode}) on the folder {where}. A whole-disk copy has each partition in a subfolder of its own (p1-vfat, p3-btrfs…).
tools_verify_bad: The backup is damaged: checksums do not match for {bad} of {blocks}.
tools_mount_desc: The image is attached as a disk; the volumes inside get drive letters and open in File Explorer.
tools_verify_desc: Checks every block's checksum against the metadata in the image (or the .obkm file).
tools_letters_desc: The EFI system partition, the Windows recovery environment and vendor partitions. Windows gives them no letter on its own — here you can assign one so the partition shows up in Explorer, and remove it when it is no longer needed.
tools_letters_note: Explorer opens the EFI partition only as an administrator. Do not keep the letters for long: Windows and its updates expect these partitions to stay hidden.
tools_letters_none: No hidden partitions with a Windows filesystem were found.
tools_letters_assigned: The partition now has the letter {letter}:
boot_copy_not_durable: The copy of the previous state went to a temporary disk ({path}) and will not survive a restart. Save it yourself if you may need it.
boot_delete_confirm_file: The loader {file} stays on the partition — only the entry pointing to it is deleted.
boot_not_uefi: This computer does not boot through UEFI.
boot_priority_desc: The order in which the firmware tries the loaders. In its settings this is “Boot priority”, Boot Option #1, #2 and so on. Click a name to edit it.
boot_partly_parsed: not fully parsed, cannot be edited
boot_not_in_menu: Entries outside the menu: {n}. They exist, but the firmware does not offer them.
boot_one_time_menu_note: The one-time boot menu you open with a key at power-on may list the same entries in a different order — the firmware builds it its own way, and it does not affect the priority.
boot_stored_in_firmware_note: Boot entries are stored in the motherboard's memory, not on a disk, so a partition backup does not keep them. Before every change a copy is saved to {dir}.
boot_orphans_desc: The files are in place, but no entry points to them — they are not in the firmware boot menu.
boot_no_orphans: Everything on the EFI partitions has an entry pointing to it.
boot_esps_desc: Where the loaders themselves are stored.
boot_unavailable: The service does not read the UEFI boot entries on this system. They can be viewed and changed with efibootmgr.
bmc_desc: Media from which you can back up a system while it is shut down and restore it back — including the disk the system boots from. The result is an ISO file: write it to a USB stick or attach it as a drive in a virtual machine.
bmc_tab_windows: Based on Microsoft Windows Recovery Environment (x64)
bmc_on_media: Bootable media can only be built from an installed Windows. Here, on the media itself, there is neither this machine's driver store nor room to unpack the image:
bmc_on_media_hint: Run the program in a regular Windows to build the media.
bmc_windows_desc: Built from what is already on this machine: Windows Recovery Environment, the program with its interface, the WebView2 runtime and, optionally, this computer's drivers. Native NTFS and ReFS, no VSS snapshot needed — the system on the disk being backed up is shut down.
bmc_windows_needs_windows: A medium based on the Windows Recovery Environment can only be built on Windows: it needs DISM and Windows' own files.
bmc_click_to_build: Click to set up and build →
bmc_no_winre: The recovery environment image was not found. Enable it with
bmc_no_winre_or: or take Winre.wim from a Windows installation image.
bmc_linux_desc: A minimal system with a kernel, disk and network drivers, and the same program. Needs no Windows to build and reads ext4, btrfs, XFS and LUKS directly — for machines without Windows and for disks whose layout is easier to handle from Linux.
bmc_on_media_linux: A new medium cannot be built here, on the medium itself: the system runs from this stick, and a new medium is built by the program installed on Linux.
bmc_linux_build: The program builds the ISO itself — Debian 13, UEFI with Secure Boot and BIOS — and saves it into a folder you choose; if you like, it writes it onto a USB stick right away.
bmc_linux_download_win: It is built on Linux only; here the ready ISO of this version is downloaded from GitHub and checked against the release's checksum.
lmb_intro: The image carries Debian 13, a kernel with disk and network drivers, and Own Backup with its window — exactly the version installed on this computer.
lmb_intro_win: The image holds Debian 13, a kernel with disk and network drivers, and Own Backup with its interface, the same version as this program. It can be built on Linux only, so here the ready ISO is downloaded from the GitHub release.
lmb_needs: Needs the internet: about 1 GB of Debian packages is downloaded. The build runs in a temporary folder in {dir} (about 10 GiB), removed as soon as the build ends. The build takes about 15 minutes; the program asks for an administrator password.
lmb_to_stick_note: After the build the ISO is written onto the chosen stick, read back to verify it and given a partition for the logs. Everything on the stick is erased.
lmb_write_ready: Write a ready ISO onto a stick…
lmb_rep_note: Write the ISO onto a stick ("Write a ready ISO onto a stick…" or any image writer) or attach it as a drive in a virtual machine. Secure Boot need not be turned off.
lmb_rep_note_win: Write the ISO to a stick with a program that writes the image whole, byte for byte (Rufus in DD mode, for example), or attach it as a drive in a virtual machine. On Windows this program cannot write a stick for the Linux medium yet. Secure Boot need not be turned off.
lmb_choose: How do you want to get the medium?
lmb_way_download: Download the ready ISO from GitHub
lmb_way_download_note: The medium of version {version} from the release {tag}, {size}. A few minutes, no administrator password.
lmb_way_download_looking: Looking for the ready ISO on GitHub…
lmb_way_download_none: There is no ready ISO for the installed version on GitHub.
lmb_way_download_none_win: There is no ready ISO for this version of the program on GitHub.
lmb_way_build_note: About 15 minutes: about 1 GB of Debian packages is downloaded and about 10 GiB used for a while; needs an administrator password.
lmb_dl_intro: The medium of version {version} is downloaded from the release {tag} on GitHub ({size}) and checked against the release's checksum. Until it is checked, it sits in the folder under a hidden temporary name.
lmb_dl_intro_win: The medium of version {version} will be downloaded from the release {tag} on GitHub ({size}) and checked against the release's checksum. Until it is checked, the file sits in the folder under a temporary name ending in .part.
ms_head: Write the Linux medium onto a stick
ms_intro: A ready medium image (ISO) built by this program is written onto the whole stick.
ms_intro_write: It is then read back to verify it and given an OBK-LOGS partition where the medium keeps its logs.
ms_no_sticks: No USB sticks, memory cards or removable disks. Insert a stick and click Refresh.
ms_mounted: mounted ({mounts}) — eject it in the file manager without unplugging it
ms_rep_note: Boot from the stick by choosing it in the computer's boot menu. Secure Boot does not need to be turned off.
mb_head_windows: Media based on Windows Recovery Environment
mb_intro_win: The image will include: Windows Recovery Environment, the Own Backup program (interface, engine, command line), the WebView2 runtime for the interface and the system libraries WinPE lacks.
mb_intro_win_build: The image will include: Windows Recovery Environment (build {build}, {language}), the Own Backup program (interface, engine, command line), the WebView2 runtime for the interface and the system libraries WinPE lacks.
mb_intro_win_boot: The media boots straight into the program; from it you can back up a system while it is shut down and restore it back.
mb_compress_on_note: the ISO file is about 280 MB smaller, but at boot the runtime takes about 260 MB of RAM — WinPE keeps the whole image in memory
mb_compress_off_note: the runtime sits on the media uncompressed: the ISO is bigger, but memory stays free at boot — files are read as needed
mb_add_drivers_note: without them the media may not see the disks: that is exactly why “universal” media cannot find NVMe and RAID
mb_polling_hw: Polling hardware: disks and network adapters…
mb_no_hw: No disks or network adapters on this machine need a driver.
mb_inbox_all: This machine's disks and network run on drivers built into Windows — there is no need to export them.
mb_inbox_rest: The other devices run on drivers built into Windows — there is no need to export them.
mb_inbox_check: The build checks that they are in the recovery environment too; any that is missing is added from this machine.
mb_tools_note: programs from this computer, along with their settings
lmb_tools_note: Krusader, a two-panel file manager, and FeatherPad, a text editor, in the medium's Start menu. Installed from Debian's packages during the build; the medium grows by about {size}.
mb_screen_text: The screen mode is chosen by the computer's firmware at boot; no video drivers are needed for it. For the media to open in the resolution the monitor recommends, turn off the CSM module in the BIOS/UEFI settings (Compatibility Support Module — usually in the boot section, “Launch CSM” or “CSM Support”). With CSM on, the screen may stay at 1024×768 or 1280×1024.
mb_screen_warn: If this computer's main system is installed in Legacy (MBR) mode, it will not boot without CSM — turn it back on when you are done with the media.
mb_rep_note: Write the ISO to a USB stick (Rufus or similar) or attach it as a drive in a virtual machine.
about_description: Backups of whole disks and volumes, block by block: only used clusters go into a backup, and excluded files do not go in at all. A backup can be encrypted with a password. From a backup you can restore a partition, a disk or individual files — and, from bootable media, even the disk the system boots from.
about_link_media: named pipe {pipe}; the service runs as a boot media process
about_link_service: named pipe {pipe} with restricted access (no network port is open)
about_link_socket: Unix socket {path}: open to the own-backup group from an active local session, and to root (no network port is open)
about_link_socket_media: Unix socket {path}; the service runs as a boot media process
about_svc_media: boot media mode: the service runs as a process and is not installed in the system
about_svc_refused: responding, but refuses this window — an active local session or root is needed
about_svc_not_responding: installed but not responding — check that it is running
about_format_value: VHDX, qcow2 (zstd compression) or OBK — encrypted (zstd and AES-256-GCM)
about_checksums_value: xxHash64 for every block, in the manifest inside the image
about_licence_terms: The program is free to use for noncommercial purposes — at home, in education, in research; the source code is available to study and modify, and derivative works stay under the same terms.
about_licence_commercial: Commercial use requires a separate license — its terms are in COMMERCIAL-LICENSE.txt next to the program.
about_licence_osi: This is not an “open source” license in the OSI sense: the right words are “source-available, free for noncommercial use”. Third-party components and their licenses are listed in
about_hint_activity: The “Activity” section keeps every run — it shows how each one ended and with what error.
about_hint_logs: Details are in the logs in the Logs folder next to the program: own-backup-service-YYYY-MM-DD.log and own-backup-gui-YYYY-MM-DD.log, one file per day, kept for 30 days. Times in them are in UTC. To get to the bottom of an error, turn on the verbose log level in “Settings” and try again.
about_hint_logs_linux: Details are in the logs: the service writes to {service} (own-backup-service-YYYY-MM-DD.log), the window and the command line to {ui} (own-backup-gui-…, own-backup-cli-…). One file per day, kept for 30 days; times in them are in UTC. To get to the bottom of an error, turn on the verbose log level in “Settings” and try again.
about_hint_mirror: In “Settings” you can mirror the log to a USB stick or another disk — it survives even if a restore takes away the disk the regular log is on.
about_hint_media: A system that does not boot can be restored from bootable media: “Tools” → “Bootable media”.
act_empty: The history of backups and restores will appear here.
akey_preparing: Preparing the job's key — this takes a few seconds.
akey_write_down: Write down the recovery key now. It is shown once and stored nowhere — not by us, not by the service.
akey_confirm_label: Type the recovery key to confirm:
akey_not_saved_yet: Until it is entered, nothing is saved: the job stays unencrypted.
aunl_what: To open {name}, you need the backup password or the recovery key.
aunl_password_note: The password that was set when encryption was turned on for this job.
aunl_recovery_note: The string the program showed once when encryption was turned on. Spaces and letter case do not matter.
aunl_busy_note: Deriving the key takes a few seconds — by design: that is what makes guessing the password expensive.
pwf_layout_title: Keyboard layout: {name}. Switch with Alt+Shift or Win+Space.
pwf_caps_on: Caps Lock is on — letters are typed in capitals
pwf_caps_unknown: Caps Lock: known after the first key press
wiz_verify_schedule_hint: When unchecked, verifies the latest version of each source together with its parents. Results appear in Activity.
wiz_vhdx_note_linux: Windows itself opens the backup with a double click, and Own Backup mounts it here too. No compression — the file is bigger.
wiz_method_only_full: On this system the service makes full backups only for now; incremental and differential chains will come later.
wiz_method_chain_formats: Chains (incremental and differential backups) are written here only in: {formats}.
wiz_adv_enc_unavailable: Encrypted archives (OBK) are not available on this system yet: the service has no key store here.
wiz_excl_unavailable: On this system the service does not exclude files yet: a volume backup holds all of its files.
wiz_adv_unavailable: The speed limit, low priority and the action after the backup are not carried out by the service on this system yet.
wiz_dest_on_source: The destination folder is on a volume being backed up ({source}). The backup would grow along with its source — choose a folder on another volume.
wiz_dest_cannot_tell: The service could not check where the destination folder is: {reason}. It checks again before the run and does not start the backup until it is sure.
wiz_key_store_unknown: It could not be told whether the service key directory is on {source}: {reason}. The copy is made only if that directory can be left out by a file scan; a sector-by-sector copy and a copy of a filesystem that cannot be scanned are refused.
wiz_volumes_separate: Each selected volume becomes a separate backup file: the service's engine on this system does not write a whole-disk copy as one image.
wiz_volumes_separate_no_id: This disk has no persistent name in /dev/disk/by-id (a virtual disk without a serial number or a loop device has none), and its kernel name may belong to another disk after a reboot. So each selected volume becomes a separate backup file.
wiz_err_event_unsupported: The service does not watch this event on this system — choose another one.
rd_target_running_hidden: The disk of the running system ({disks}) is not offered here: it is restored from the boot medium.
app_not_in_group: The service is running, but your user is not in the own-backup group, so the window cannot connect to it. Add it: sudo usermod -aG own-backup $USER — then sign out, sign in again and click “Retry”.
app_relogin_group: Your user is already in the own-backup group, but this session started earlier and does not have it yet, so the window cannot connect to the service. Sign out, sign in again and click “Retry”.
tools_mount_desc_linux: The image is mounted read-only; its volume is mounted into a folder and opens in the file manager.
jmt_intro_linux: The chosen version is mounted read-only and its volume is mounted into a folder. The “Tools” section opens — the image is unmounted there too.
eng_no_volumes_linux: No volume was found. Details are in the logs (their folders are named in “About”).
about_licence_commercial_linux: Commercial use requires a separate license — its terms are in the COMMERCIAL-LICENSE file in /usr/share/doc/own-backup.
